name: GEF Small Grants Programme (CEPF-executed countries)
summary: GEF Small Grants run by CEPF for Conservation International in Equatorial Guinea, Libya and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, giving grants of up to US$75,000 to registered civil society organisations through competitive calls.

amount.note: Upper limit; a lower limit may be set for individual calls

steps: Eligibility screening and preliminary technical review

eligibility.rule: Is legally registered in the country in question
Has a bank account that accepts foreign-currency wire transfers
Government-owned applicants are independent, can receive private funds and cannot claim sovereign immunity
Implements no more than one SGP grant at a time during a GEF Operational Phase
Targets the relevant Country Program Strategy's thematic and geographic priorities
Does not fund land purchases, physical resettlement or potential harm to critical habitat
Does not fund activities prohibited by CEPF environmental and social safeguards

administered_by.quote: with the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) serving as its executing agency.

applicant_types.quote: Civil society organizations (CSOs) are eligible to receive an SGP grant if they: (a) are legally registered in the country in question;

geography.quote: the CI/CEPF team will implement the SGP in five countries: Equatorial Guinea Libya Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Sri Lanka Turkmenistan

access.quote: Regular SGP grants are solicited through competitive, open calls.

amount.quote: Regular SGP grants have an upper limit of US$75,000, although a lower limit may be set for individual calls for proposals.

window.quote: It is anticipated that there will be at least one call for proposals in each country in both 2026 and 2027.

effort.quote: Applicants should prepare a Letter of Inquiry (LOI), following the template for the relevant country, in one of the languages specified in the call for proposals.
All LOIs submitted will first be screened to confirm their eligibility. Eligible LOIs will then undergo preliminary technical review.
shortlisted applications will be further considered during a meeting of the National Steering Committee (NSC) for the country in question
organizations whose LOIs are selected will be invited to submit full project proposals

eligibility.quote: are legally registered in the country in question
have a bank account in the organization's name that can receive payments by wire transfer in foreign currency

the enterprise or institution has a legal personality independent of any government agency or actor, that the enterprise or institution has the authority to apply for and receive private funds in its own name and capacity, and that the enterprise or institution may not assert a claim of sovereign immunity.
Any given CSO is permitted to implement no more than one SGP grant at a time during a GEF Operational Phase.
Proposed activities must target the thematic and geographic priorities set out in the relevant Country Program Strategy.
Grants must not be used for the purchase of land, physical resettlement of people or activities that have the potential to cause adverse impacts to critical habitat.
Grants must not be used for any other activities prohibited by CEPF's environmental and social safeguard policies.

after_award.quote: Grantees submit evidence of milestone completion throughout the life of the grant.
At project completion, all grantees are required to submit a Final Completion and Impact Report, following the template in Annex 1, within two months of the project end date.
The National Coordinator, accompanied, in some cases, by CEPF staff, conducts site visits to selected grants
